questions.evidence:
Leo helps with the washing on Sunday. He places all the clean clothes on the line, including his sister's wool sweater. The sweater is heavy with water, and its sleeves stretch lower than the shirts beside it. His sister notices before leaving for basketball.

She checks the care label inside the sweater. It says to dry the garment flat. She explains that the label gives instructions for this particular item. The instructions on the cotton shirts do not automatically apply to the sweater too.

Together, they move the sweater onto a clean towel on a flat drying rack. Leo writes a small reminder and clips it above the washing machine. He does not write all clothes dry flat; he writes check each care label first.

A week later, Leo washes another load and sorts the items by their care instructions. He finishes a little more slowly, but nobody has to move wet clothes twice. The reminder helps because it directs him to information instead of making an oversized rule.
